newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill yield seen below market at auction.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill yield seen below market at auction.

text.p: The average yield at Wednesday's auction of 7.50 trillion roubles of 266-day GKO discount Treasury bills (series 22068) is likely to be below current market levels, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said there were plenty of funds in the market and there was no reason to speculate on a rise in yields.
A poll of 18 dealers put the average yield in a range from 31.74 to 36.14 percent.
The average price for a new 3.00 trillion rouble tranche of 18-month bonds (series 24010) was seen in a 80.20-100.10 range, the poll showed.
The series 22067 bills, maturing October 1 closed on Tuesday with an average yield of 33.66 percent.
Earlier tranches of the 24010 bonds closed at 100.15 percent, yielding 36.26.
"Non-residents are displaying plenty of activity, so it's hardly worth expecting a yield above market levels," said Most Bank dealer Andrei Popov.

The guaranteed dollar yield for non-residents investing in the government securities market falls to 12.5 from 13.0 percent on January 16, so Wednesday is the last opportunity for foreigners to lock in the higher yield.

At the same time the Finance Ministry has no longer been simply rolling over maturing issues at recent auctions, but funding itself as well, which would put upwards pressure on yields if it continues on Wednesday, dealers said.
The average yield fell on Tuesday to 33.1 from 33.4 percent on Monday, with turnover rising to 3.68 trillion from 3.24 trillion roubles.
